ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
ETC is the abbreviation for Electronic Toll Collection system. Recently, the traffic speed at an ETC lane in Chongqing has increased from $20\mathrm{km/h}$ to $40\mathrm{km/h}$. The process of a car passing through the ETC lane is shown in the figure. For simplicity of calculation, assume that a car travels at a constant velocity of $\mathrm{v}_{0}=30\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ towards the toll station along a straight line. If it passes through the ETC lane, it needs to decelerate uniformly to $\mathrm{v}_{1}=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ exactly $d=10\mathrm{m}$ before the center line of the toll station, then pass through the center line at constant velocity, and finally accelerate uniformly back to $\mathrm{v}_{0}$ for normal driving. Assume the magnitude of the car's acceleration and deceleration is $1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ in both processes, and neglect the length of the car body.

1. What is the magnitude of the displacement of the car during the process from the start of deceleration to the restoration of normal driving speed while passing through the ETC lane?
2. If the car passes through the constant velocity section at a velocity of $\mathrm{v}_{2}=10\mathrm{m/s}$, with other conditions unchanged, what is the time saved by the car during the process of passing through the ETC lane after the speed increase, compared to before the speed increase?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ETC lane, with the vehicle traveling direction from left to right. In the figure, two vertical dashed lines mark a section of “Constant speed zone” (constant-speed zone), and the right dashed line is labeled “Toll booth centerline” (toll booth centerline). The distance from the left dashed line to the toll booth centerline is marked as d=10 m, indicating that the vehicle enters the constant-speed passing area 10 m before reaching the centerline. Reasoning: According to the problem and the figure, divide the motion into three sections: first uniformly decelerate from v0=30 m/s to the ETC constant speed, then pass through the toll booth centerline within the constant-speed zone of d=10 m, and finally uniformly accelerate back to v0=30 m/s. The magnitudes of acceleration and deceleration are both 1 m/s^2. Question 1: The original constant passing speed is v1=5 m/s. The deceleration distance satisfies v1^2-v0^2=2as, where the deceleration acceleration is -1 m/s^2, so s_dec=(v0^2-v1^2)/(2×1)=(30^2-5^2)/2=(900-25)/2=437.5 m. The acceleration section recovers from 5 m/s to 30 m/s, and the distance is the same, 437.5 m. The total displacement is s=437.5+10+437.5=885 m. Question 2: Compare the passing time within the same section of 885 m. When originally v1=5 m/s, the deceleration time is (30-5)/1=25 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/5=2 s, and the acceleration time is 25 s, so the old total time t_old=25+2+25=52 s. After the speed is increased, the constant passing speed v2=10 m/s. The deceleration distance is (30^2-10^2)/2=(900-100)/2=400 m, and the acceleration distance is also 400 m; the constant-speed zone is still 10 m, therefore the new ETC core process distance is 400+10+400=810 m, which is 75 m less than the original 885 m. The extra 75 m is traveled at the normal speed v0=30 m/s, and the time is 75/30=2.5 s. The new process deceleration time is (30-10)/1=20 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/10=1 s, and the acceleration time is 20 s, so the new total time t_new=20+1+20+2.5=43.5 s. The saved time Δt=52-43.5=8.5 s.

If it passes through the ETC lane, it needs to decelerate uniformly to $v_1=5\mathrm{m/s}$ exactly $d=10\mathrm{m}$ before the center line of the toll station, then pass through the center line at constant velocity, and finally accelerate uniformly back to $v_0$ for normal driving. 1. What is the magnitude of the displacement of the car from the start of deceleration to the restoration of normal driving speed while passing through the ETC lane?

method.method_draft: Segment the motion according to the diagram: a deceleration segment before the dashed constant-speed zone, a constant-speed segment of length d=10 m ending at the toll booth centerline, and an acceleration segment after the centerline. From the text, use v0=30 m/s, old ETC speed v1=5 m/s, |a|=1 m/s^2. For part 1, compute the deceleration distance by v1^2-v0^2=2as, giving s_dec=(v0^2-v1^2)/(2a); the acceleration distance back to v0 is equal by symmetry. Add s_dec+d+s_acc to get 885 m. For part 2, compute the old time over this same 885 m interval: deceleration time (30-5)/1, constant-zone time 10/5, acceleration time (30-5)/1. For the new speed v2=10 m/s, compute the new deceleration/acceleration distances and times; the new ETC-core distance is shorter than 885 m, so include the remaining distance within the same old start/end interval as normal driving at v0=30 m/s. Subtract the new total time from the old total time to obtain 8.5 s saved.

图像描述：图中是一条ETC车道，车辆行驶方向由左向右。图中用两条竖直虚线标出一段“Constant speed zone”（匀速区），右侧虚线处标注为“Toll booth centerline”（收费站中心线）。从左侧虚线到收费站中心线的距离标为 d=10 m，表示车辆在到达中心线前10 m进入匀速通过区域。

推理：按题目和图示把运动分成三段：先从 v0=30 m/s 匀减速到 ETC 匀速速度，再在 d=10 m 的匀速区内通过收费站中心线，最后匀加速恢复到 v0=30 m/s。加速度、减速度大小均为 1 m/s^2。

第1问：原来匀速通过速度为 v1=5 m/s。减速距离满足 v1^2-v0^2=2as，其中减速加速度为 -1 m/s^2，所以 s_dec=(v0^2-v1^2)/(2×1)=(30^2-5^2)/2=(900-25)/2=437.5 m。加速段从 5 m/s 恢复到 30 m/s，距离相同，为 437.5 m。总位移为 s=437.5+10+437.5=885 m。

第2问：比较同一段 885 m 内的通过时间。原来 v1=5 m/s 时，减速时间为 (30-5)/1=25 s，匀速区时间为 10/5=2 s，加速时间为 25 s，所以旧总时间 t_old=25+2+25=52 s。

速度提高后，匀速通过速度 v2=10 m/s。减速距离为 (30^2-10^2)/2=(900-100)/2=400 m，加速距离同为 400 m，匀速区仍为 10 m，因此新ETC核心过程距离为 400+10+400=810 m，比原来的 885 m 少 75 m。少出的 75 m 按正常速度 v0=30 m/s 行驶，时间为 75/30=2.5 s。新过程减速时间为 (30-10)/1=20 s，匀速区时间为 10/10=1 s，加速时间为 20 s，所以新总时间 t_new=20+1+20+2.5=43.5 s。节省时间 Δt=52-43.5=8.5 s。

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一条 ETC 车道，车辆沿图示“Driving direction”向前行驶。车道中间标出了“Constant speed zone”（匀速区），匀速区左端到右侧“Toll booth centerline”（收费站中心线）的距离标为 d=10 m。也就是说，车先减速，到达距中心线 10 m 处后进入匀速区，通过中心线后再加速恢复正常速度。

推理：按速度—时间图理解，过程分三段：速度斜线下降的匀减速段、低速水平线对应的 10 m 匀速段、速度斜线上升的匀加速段。

1. 原来低速通过速度 v1=5 m/s。由 v0=30 m/s 减到 5 m/s，加速度大小为 1 m/s^2，所以减速时间为 (30-5)/1=25 s。减速段位移等于速度—时间图梯形面积：[(30+5)/2]×25=437.5 m。加速段从 5 m/s 恢复到 30 m/s，同理时间也是 25 s，位移也是 437.5 m。中间匀速区长度为 10 m。因此总位移为 437.5+10+437.5=885 m。

2. 提速后匀速通过速度 v2=10 m/s。减速从 30 m/s 到 10 m/s，时间为 (30-10)/1=20 s，减速段位移为 [(30+10)/2]×20=400 m。10 m 匀速段所用时间为 10/10=1 s。加速段同理位移为 400 m，时间为 20 s。新过程核心位移为 400+10+400=810 m。为了与原来的 885 m 区间比较，还差 885-810=75 m，这 75 m 以正常速度 30 m/s 行驶，时间为 75/30=2.5 s。原过程总时间为 25+10/5+25=52 s；新过程总时间为 20+1+20+2.5=43.5 s。所以节省时间为 52-43.5=8.5 s。

From the image, take the constant-speed part as a fixed 10 m zone before/through the centerline, with identical approach and departure acceleration magnitudes on either side. For part 1, because deceleration from 30 to 5 and acceleration from 5 to 30 are symmetric, each takes 25 s and each has average speed (30+5)/2=17.5 m/s, so each covers 437.5 m; add the 10 m zone to get 885 m. For part 2, compare the old and new cases by changes: raising the low speed from 5 to 10 shortens deceleration by 5 s and acceleration by 5 s, and shortens the 10 m constant-zone time from 2 s to 1 s, giving an apparent 11 s reduction. But the higher minimum speed also shortens the deceleration-plus-acceleration distances: old two ramp distances total 875 m, new two ramp distances total 800 m, a difference of 75 m. Over the common old start/end interval, that 75 m is instead traveled normally at 30 m/s, which takes 2.5 s and must be added back. Therefore the net saving is 11-2.5=8.5 s.

按指定方法，把图中的恒速段看作固定的 10 m 区域。第 1 问：汽车从 v0=30 m/s 匀减速到 v1=5 m/s，加速度大小为 1 m/s²，所以减速时间为 (30-5)/1=25 s；减速段平均速度为 (30+5)/2=17.5 m/s，位移为 17.5×25=437.5 m。之后以 5 m/s 通过 10 m 恒速段。再由 5 m/s 匀加速到 30 m/s，与减速过程对称，时间也是 25 s，位移也是 437.5 m。因此总位移为 437.5+10+437.5=885 m。

raw_record.original_question:
ETC is the abbreviation for Electronic Toll Collection system. Recently, the traffic speed at an ETC lane in Chongqing has increased from $20\mathrm{km/h}$ to $40\mathrm{km/h}$. The process of a car passing through the ETC lane is shown in the figure. For simplicity of calculation, assume that a car travels at a constant velocity of $v_0=30\mathrm{m/s}$ toward the toll station along a straight line. If it passes through the ETC lane, it needs to decelerate uniformly to $v_1=5\mathrm{m/s}$ exactly $d=10\mathrm{m}$ before the center line of the toll station, then pass through the center line at constant velocity, and finally accelerate uniformly back to $v_0$ for normal driving. Assume the magnitudes of acceleration and deceleration are both $1\mathrm{m/s^2}$, and neglect the length of the car body.

1. What is the magnitude of the displacement of the car from the start of deceleration to the restoration of normal driving speed while passing through the ETC lane?
2. If the car passes through the constant-velocity section at $v_2=10\mathrm{m/s}$, with other conditions unchanged, what time is saved during the process of passing through the ETC lane after the speed increase compared with before the speed increase?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows an ETC lane, with the vehicle traveling direction from left to right. In the figure, two vertical dashed lines mark a section of “Constant speed zone” (constant-speed zone), and the right dashed line is labeled “Toll booth centerline” (toll booth centerline). The distance from the left dashed line to the toll booth centerline is marked as d=10 m, indicating that the vehicle enters the constant-speed passing area 10 m before reaching the centerline.

Reasoning: According to the problem and the figure, divide the motion into three sections: first uniformly decelerate from v0=30 m/s to the ETC constant speed, then pass through the toll booth centerline within the constant-speed zone of d=10 m, and finally uniformly accelerate back to v0=30 m/s. The magnitudes of acceleration and deceleration are both 1 m/s^2.

Question 1: The original constant passing speed is v1=5 m/s. The deceleration distance satisfies v1^2-v0^2=2as, where the deceleration acceleration is -1 m/s^2, so s_dec=(v0^2-v1^2)/(2×1)=(30^2-5^2)/2=(900-25)/2=437.5 m. The acceleration section recovers from 5 m/s to 30 m/s, and the distance is the same, 437.5 m. The total displacement is s=437.5+10+437.5=885 m.

Question 2: Compare the passing time within the same section of 885 m. When originally v1=5 m/s, the deceleration time is (30-5)/1=25 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/5=2 s, and the acceleration time is 25 s, so the old total time t_old=25+2+25=52 s.

After the speed is increased, the constant passing speed v2=10 m/s. The deceleration distance is (30^2-10^2)/2=(900-100)/2=400 m, and the acceleration distance is also 400 m; the constant-speed zone is still 10 m, therefore the new ETC core process distance is 400+10+400=810 m, which is 75 m less than the original 885 m. The extra 75 m is traveled at the normal speed v0=30 m/s, and the time is 75/30=2.5 s. The new process deceleration time is (30-10)/1=20 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/10=1 s, and the acceleration time is 20 s, so the new total time t_new=20+1+20+2.5=43.5 s. The saved time Δt=52-43.5=8.5 s.

The acceleration section recovers from 5 m/s to 30 m/s, and the distance is the same, 437.5 m. The total displacement is s=437.5+10+437.5=885 m.

Question 2: Compare the passing time within the same section of 885 m. When originally v1=5 m/s, the deceleration time is (30-5)/1=25 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/5=2 s, and the acceleration time is 25 s, so the old total time t_old=25+2+25=52 s.

After the speed is increased, the constant passing speed v2=10 m/s. The deceleration distance is (30^2-10^2)/2=(900-100)/2=400 m, and the acceleration distance is also 400 m; the constant-speed zone is still 10 m, therefore the new ETC core process distance is 400+10+400=810 m, which is 75 m less than the original 885 m. The extra 75 m is traveled at the normal speed v0=30 m/s, and the time is 75/30=2.5 s. The new process deceleration time is (30-10)/1=20 s, the constant-speed zone time is 10/10=1 s, and the acceleration time is 20 s, so the new total time t_new=20+1+20+2.5=43.5 s. The saved time Δt=52-43.5=8.5 s.
